qp_dispositions.rationale: Direct recognition of whether entries are real is definition-level classification; no distinct multi-step JEE reasoning mechanism is present in the source possibility.

A parameterized matrix can require simultaneous constraints from multiple entries; extracting and solving all reality conditions is a reusable parameter-constraint mechanism. Candidate only; academic approval and question-level validation remain pending.
For real matrices, entrywise addition and subtraction preserve real entries directly. This is a basic closure fact and does not justify a separate archetype from the stated possibility.

Products and integer powers of real matrices remain real by entrywise closure under multiplication and addition. The stated possibility is a direct closure check without a distinct reasoning mechanism.

Determining when a linear combination of real matrices remains real can require constraints on complex scalar coefficients and matrix linear independence; this differs from imposing reality conditions on matrix entries themselves. Candidate only; validate against representative JEE questions before approval.
Transpose only reorders the entries of a real matrix, so realness is preserved directly. This is a definition-level closure property rather than a distinct JEE archetype.

For a real matrix, entrywise conjugation leaves every entry unchanged and the conjugate transpose reduces to the transpose. The stated possibility is direct property recognition without an independent inference mechanism.

The inverse of an invertible real matrix is real, as follows from standard inverse/determinant or linear-system properties. The source possibility states a direct closure theorem and does not by itself define a distinct JEE archetype.

Polynomial and defined rational expressions with real coefficients preserve real entries under the stated operations. This is a direct closure/property check; a richer task would require a separately specified mechanism.
Trace, determinant, minors and cofactors of a real matrix are real by their definitions as sums and products of real entries. This is direct property application, not a distinct archetype.

The inclusion chain for integer-, rational-, real- and complex-entry matrices follows entrywise from the corresponding scalar number sets. This is direct hierarchy recognition and does not justify a separate JEE archetype.

An m×n real matrix has mn independently selectable real entries by definition. Counting these parameters is a direct dimension/counting fact; a distinct linear-algebra constraint problem would need a separately specified source possibility.
Translating R^{m×n} or M_{m×n}(R) is notation recognition for the set of real matrices of fixed order. It is prerequisite knowledge rather than a distinct assessment mechanism.
Classifying a matrix as real or complex from its entries is direct definition-level recognition. It is retained as foundation content and is not a separate JEE archetype.
Taking the complex conjugate entrywise is a direct operation. Without additional constraints or a multi-step inference, the source possibility does not justify a distinct JEE archetype.
Computing a conjugate transpose is a direct entrywise conjugation-and-transposition procedure. It is prerequisite matrix manipulation and does not by itself justify a distinct archetype.
Hermitian verification compares the matrix with its conjugate transpose; this is a direct structural check and is retained as foundation material.
Skew-Hermitian verification compares the conjugate transpose with the negative matrix. It is the sign counterpart of Hermitian verification, not a separate reasoning archetype.

Unitary verification requires checking the conjugate-transpose product against the identity matrix. This is a distinct matrix-condition verification mechanism and is retained as a JEE Main candidate, pending academic review.

Solving parameter conditions for Hermitian, skew-Hermitian or unitary structure requires translating a matrix identity into coupled real/imaginary constraints. This is a distinct parameter-constraint mechanism and remains a JEE Main candidate pending academic review.
The canonical decomposition into Hermitian and skew-Hermitian components is a reusable construction with a verifiable uniqueness structure; retained as a JEE Main candidate pending academic review.
Scalar multiplication effects on Hermitian/skew-Hermitian type follow directly from conjugate-transpose identities and real/imaginary scalar conditions; this is a concise property check.
Sum/difference type outcomes are direct closure checks and can be summarized by a small operation table; no independent multi-step mechanism is justified by the source possibility alone.

Products and inverses require applying adjoint identities, reversing factor order and respecting commutativity/invertibility conditions; this is a reusable multi-step matrix-structure mechanism, retained as a JEE Main candidate.
The adjoint identities are foundational transformation rules. Memorizing or directly applying the identities alone does not establish a separate archetype from product/adjoint reasoning.

Orthonormal rows/columns provide an equivalent characterization of unitarity already represented by the conjugate-transpose identity candidate. Retain as a variation/reference, not a duplicate archetype.
Diagonal and trace constraints are direct consequences of Hermitian/skew-Hermitian definitions and overlap with the parameter-constraint candidate. No separate mechanism is justified.
The real symmetric/skew-symmetric/orthogonal correspondences are direct special cases of the complex matrix classes; this is conceptual mapping rather than a distinct assessment mechanism.
Identifying a row matrix from its one-row order is a direct shape definition and remains foundation content.
Determining row-matrix order and indexing constraints is direct dimensional interpretation; no distinct JEE reasoning mechanism is justified by the source possibility.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine parameter conditions under which a parametric matrix is a real matrix
archetypes.archetype: Simultaneous reality constraints in a parameterized matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Translate the requirement that an entire parameterized matrix is real into simultaneous zero-imaginary-part constraints on its entries, then solve the resulting parameter system.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Inspect each matrix entry; isolate its imaginary part; set every imaginary part to zero; solve the simultaneous equations; check that the resulting parameter values satisfy every entry.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine whether scalar multiplication or linear combinations yield a real matrix and identify conditions on scalar coefficients
archetypes.archetype: Reality of a linear combination of real matrices
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Determine the scalar-coefficient conditions under which a linear combination of real matrices has only real entries, using entrywise imaginary-part equations and any stated linear-independence information.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Write the imaginary parts of the scalar coefficients; form the matrix equation for the imaginary component of the combination; use the matrix independence or dependence conditions to solve for admissible coefficients; verify the result entrywise.
variation_dimensions: number of matrices in the combination
presence of zero or repeated matrices

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Verify whether a matrix is unitary
archetypes.archetype: Verify unitarity through the conjugate-transpose identity
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Test whether a square complex matrix is unitary by evaluating the conjugate-transpose product and comparing it with the identity matrix.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Confirm the matrix is square; compute the conjugate transpose; multiply in the required order; compare every entry with the identity matrix; use the result to decide unitarity.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine parameter conditions for a matrix to be Hermitian, skew-Hermitian, or unitary
archetypes.archetype: Derive parameter constraints for Hermitian, skew-Hermitian or unitary structure
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Convert a required matrix identity into simultaneous equations on unknown real and imaginary parameter components, then solve and verify the admissible parameter set.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Write the relevant identity A*=A, A*=-A or A*A=I; compute the conjugate transpose and required product; equate corresponding entries; separate real and imaginary parts; solve the coupled constraints; verify the original matrix identity.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Decompose a complex matrix into Hermitian and skew-Hermitian components
archetypes.archetype: Decompose a complex matrix into Hermitian and skew-Hermitian components
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Construct the Hermitian and skew-Hermitian parts of a complex square matrix using its adjoint, then verify that their sum recovers the original matrix.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compute A†; form H=(A+A†)/2 and K=(A−A†)/2; verify H†=H and K†=−K; verify A=H+K; use uniqueness when required.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine the resulting type under matrix product, inverse, or adjoint given operand types and commutativity constraints
archetypes.archetype: Infer product or inverse structure using adjoint reversal and commutativity
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Determine whether products or inverses preserve a Hermitian, skew-Hermitian or unitary condition by applying adjoint identities, reversing product order and checking the required commutativity or invertibility assumptions.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Write the adjoint of the product in reverse order; substitute the given operand identities; compare with the target matrix or its inverse; identify where commutativity is required; verify every assumption before concluding the resulting type.
